lesson_title: The Karoo Is a Birthday Cake Being Eaten Alive
hook_text: Those flat-topped hills on the N1? They're one landform photographed at five different ages.
clip_script: Picture the Karoo as a giant birthday cake. Soft sponge layers lying flat — that is the shale. And on top, a thin layer of icing set hard as a griddle — that is dolerite, ancient molten rock that squeezed between the layers and cooled. Now let the weather loose on it, because rain, frost and wind are children who always eat sponge first. Wherever the icing holds, the land keeps a dead-flat top. Wherever it is breached, the sponge underneath is gutted. Watch the stages. The whole slab is a plateau. Eat inward from the edges until a chunk is cut off: still flat, wider than it is tall — a mesa, Spanish for table. Keep eating until the table is taller than it is wide, a bar stool of rock — a butte. The Three Sisters beside the N1 are three of them in a row, each wearing its dolerite hard hat. Then the fatal moment: the hat is picked through, the soft rock loses its protection, and the hill rounds into a traffic cone — the pointed koppie on every Karoo postcard. And here is the strangest part: the cliffs never go soft. They march backwards instead, keeping their sharp edges for millions of years, leaving a smooth plain behind them. Table-land, table, stool, cone, flat. Five ages, one cake — and you can see all five from a car window.
visual_style: A layer cake morphing into a Karoo panorama, time-lapse erosion carving plateau to mesa to butte to cone with each name stamping on screen, the dolerite cap glowing as a hard hat until it shatters.
mood: Playful time-machine wonder over deep time.
pacing: Quick setup on the cake, rhythmic beats through the five ages, slow awe on the backwards-marching cliff.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read a hundred million years off any flat-topped hill.
